medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The five-week Summer Science Program offers an introduction to the medical school curriculum, along with reading and study skill enrichment sessions designed to strengthen students' mastery of these areas.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Academic Houses.  Over 100 Medical Student Interest groups and additional student organizations.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: One medical school, two campuses, in Little Rock and Fayetteville.  See our website at www.medicine.uams.edu for additional information on both campuses.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing available, studio apartments and one-bedroom. Extensive off-campus housing near campus in both Little Rock and Northwest AR in Fayetteville.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Student Wellness Program: The mission of the UAMS Student Wellness Program is to promote wellness in our student body by providing the tools and support to help them maintain balance in their lives and achieve their full professional and personal potential.   The SWP provides confidential assistance to actively enrolled students and their spouses who are experiencing emotional, psychological, and psychiatric problems in a timely manner.  There is no financial cost to students seeking care, except for the cost of prescription medications.  The SWP is staffed by one full time and one part-time board-certified psychiatrists and three clinical social workers.  Students must be physically located in the state of Arkansas when receiving counseling and psychiatric services through the SWP; thus students training in another state are responsible for the cost and arrangements of mental health services when outside of Arkansas. Additional information for students at both the Little Rock and Fayetteville campuses is available online at https://studentwellness.uams.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The UAMS College of Medicine strives to achieve an environment of collegiality by demonstrating the utmost respect for one another, free from disruptive, threatening, and violent behavior. We will not accept inappropriate, unprofessional, or intimidating behavior within the workplace and learning environment. All persons, including patients, visitors, staff, all students, medical residents/fellows and post-doctoral fellows, and faculty are treated with courtesy, and dignity. All faculty members, house staff members, post-doctoral fellows and all students who practice at or in affiliation with UAMS conduct themselves in a professional, collaborative, and cooperative manner consistent with the UAMS Employee Handbook, the Medical Staff Bylaws of the affiliated institutions, the UAMS House staff Handbook, College of Medicine Student Handbook, UAMS Human Resources policies.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: We do not require a driver's license, per se.  However, in this day and time every student must assume responsibility for reliable transportation to meet the obligations of medical studies and patient care.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire when engaging with patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Available in all courses and modules.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: 1st year clinical training using standardized patients in the UAMS Clinical Skills Center. Students can gain additional patient interaction at the UAMS 12th Street Health Clinic.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Traditional lectures, small groups, and  team-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students exposed to patient care in the freshman year through the ability to shadow physicians at UAMS. Clinical clerkships begin at the start of third year after taking the USMLE Step 1 exam.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Orientation is 4 days long but not a traditional prematriculation program.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance:
Team based learning in small groups must be attended in person.
All lectures can be attended in-person or viewed remotely using live-streaming.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The  Student Centered Curriculum is a new direction for medical student education in Arkansas and emphasizes student centered, active learning principles.  In addition, the revised curriculum emphasizes content integration and activities to promote better understanding, relevance and retention. Problem solving and critical thinking activities to promote deeper contextual understanding, sometimes neglected in most lecture based curricula, will be the focal point of the Student Centered Curriculum.  The third year is a full 48 weeks with rotation through the major clinical services. This expanded clinical year provides substantial preparation for the predominantly elective fourth year, which consists of a minimum of 32 weeks to a maximum of 48 weeks of courses selected with the assistance of a faculty advisor. On and off-campus electives are available to round out preparation for each student's career goals. Opportunities are provided for students to engage in research activities in many of the clinical departmental and within our Biomedical Reseach Institute.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The University of Arkansas College of Medicine is recognized nationally for emphasizing the critical importance of primary care specialties.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
All medical students can pursue research opportunities in clinical departments and in the Biomedical Science areas of the Graduate School for non-clinical research.
University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) and its affiliate research institutions saw research funding grow this past year, with $203.1 million in grants by June 30, 2022, the end of the state’s fiscal year.  Reported on Dec. 14, 2022  UAMS News
The bulk of UAMS’ external research grant funding is from NIH and other federal sources.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The M1 and M2 courses are Pass/Fail.  Scores are documented to provide class-rank information (per Quartile) at the time of  Residency Program application.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service is highly recommended and the majority of students are involved in outreach programs in the Little Rock, Fayetteville/NW AR region, and rural areas of Arkansas.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students can choose to participate in the Honors in Research track.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Affiliated hospitals: two Veterans Administration hospitals and AR Children's Hospital in Little Rock and Fayetteville at regional hospitals, a VA medical center and a new AR Children's Hospital.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: On October 7, 1879 the medical school opened its doors to 22 eager students. From these humble beginnings grew the excellence and prestige now embodied in the College of Medicine. Today, the College of Medicine has over 1000 full-time and part-time faculty, over 600 residents, and over 600 medical students. UAMS is Arkansas' only institution of professional and graduate education devoted solely to the health and biological sciences. In fulfilling its educational mission, the College of Medicine, in conjunction with the UAMS Medical Center, provides the environment and opportunities for students and practitioners alike to learn and maintain the knowledge and skills required in the 21st century.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: To improve health and increase knowledge through innovative teaching, ground-breaking research, state-of-the-art patient care and outstanding service to Arkansas, our nation and the world. The UAMS College of Medicine leads the way in educating exemplary physicians and translating biomedical discovery into innovative treatments that enable our health care teams to deliver superior medical care.  The mission is to improve the health, health care and well-being of Arkansans, others in the region,  the nation and other countries in the world by educating current and future health professionals and the public. By providing high quality, innovative patent- and family-centered health care as well as specialty expertise not routinely available in smaller community settings. Core values include commitment to diversity and health equity supported by diversity of UAMS leadership, faculty, staff, and learners to reduce health care disparities in our state, and honor the unique contributions provided by a diversity of values, beliefs, and cultures.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks from the time notification was sent through USPS. The Preferred Address on AMCAS must be up to date.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: If the applicant's college has a Premedical Advisory Committee (PMAC), the premedical committee letter is MANDATORY up until 2 years post-graduation. It is the applicant's responsibility to know the deadlines and requirements to receive a committee letter from their respective schools.  If the applicant's college does not have a PMAC committee, or if it has been more than two years since the applicant last attended college for any reason, the applicant must have academic letters from three professors familiar with the applicant's classroom performance. If it has been more than 2 years since graduating and the Premedical Advisory Committee from the school you attended is willing to write a committee letter, we will accept that as well.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: In addition to the required Premedical Advisory Committee letter (outlined below), applicants are encouraged to request an additional 3 (maximum) letters written by professors, research advisors, physicians you have shadowed or worked with, advisors for student organizations you have been an officer in and/or employers.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Most interviews are in-person, but we also offer a virtual interview day for applicants who cannot interview in person.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Arkansas applicants must have a 500 or greater MCAT score and non-Arkansas residents a 505 or greater to be invited to submit a secondary application and be invited for a faculty interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: "Blind" interviews on scheduled interview dates in September through January.  Some interviews will be conducted on weekdays while other interview days will be on Saturdays.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Most interviews are conducted on the UAMS Little Rock campus.  Some interviews are conducted at the Northwest UAMS campus in Fayetteville.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Most interviews are in-person, but we also offer a virtual interview day for applicants who cannot interview in-person.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: The link to our secondary application is sent to medical school applicants who meet the admissions standards
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Applicants must either be U.S. Citizens or have Permanent Resident status  with a valid I-155 (Green card) at the time of submitting the AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Applicants with strong ties to Arkansas.   Applicants from border states pay in-state tuition, out of state tuition is waived.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: Tom South, Assistant Dean of Medical Student Admissions
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: The UAMS College of Medicine Admissions Committee has 15 members appointed by the Dean of the College of Medicine and approved by the University of Arkansa Board of Trustees. The committee is the only body with authority to make admissions decisions.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: UAMS conducts a holistic review process. Although MCAT scores are looked at, other factors are taken into consideration.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: However, applicants with less than a 3.0 undergraduate GPA are unlikely to receive serious consideration.  Applicants would be encouraged to continue their preparation for medical school by successfully completing a master's degree or post bacc program.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Undergraduate GPAs are considered but we do not have a minimum cut-off. Applicants with an overall cumulative undergraduate GPA or graduate GPA of less than 3.0 are at a significant disadvantage.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours needed for postbacc or graduate coursework, but at least one semester of coursework with approximately 12 credit hours.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Although we accept courses successfully competed at a community college to satisfy some of our pre-matriculation course requirements, applicants should complete the bulk of their undergraduate coursework at a four-year, degree granting college of university.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants who may wish to submit an update to their application after submitting the AMCAS application may do so.  However, any update is limited to a one-time, one-page only document sent to the Admissions Office as an email attachment.  The deadline to receive all updates is January 15, 2027.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: An applicant's financial status is not a factor in selection for admission. The Rural Practice Programs allow Arkansas residents who commit to practice primary care medicine in rural communities in Arkansas to receive loans during medical school. The student is obligated to return to a rural community following residency training and to practice full time for the same number of years the student was assisted during medical school. For each year of service, one year of loans is forgiven until the debt is retired. A unique feature of the Rural Practice Programs allows Arkansas residents on the Alternate List, who are willing to practice full-time in a rural community in Arkansas, to interview with the Arkansas Rural Medical Practice Student Loan and Scholarship Board. If the Board approves the alternate's Rural Practice Program application, the applicant is advanced to the top of the alternate list.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Applicants can use "Plan to Enroll" on AMCAS beginning February 19, 2026

By April 15, 2026 Applicants holding more than three acceptances are asked to narrow their acceptance offers to three. They can retain their status for any schools that they might be on alternate list for.

The option of "Commit to enroll" becomes available on April 30, 2026. At this point applicants have the option to choose Commit to Enroll indicating a final selection has been made and withdrawn their applications from all other schools by informing each school directly of their decision to withdraw.
Must choose "Commit to Enroll" by June 30, 2026

medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: After an applicant is offered a position in the entering freshman 4-Year MD class, the accepted applicant must submit a subsequent application to be considered for the accelerated Three-Year MD program
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Approximately the last week in April
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: They apply and are accepted to the 4 year regular MD program.  Then, there is a separate process/application for the 3 year track.  An applicant who has not been accepted can’t apply specifically to the 3 year program.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Must commit to practice primary care, i.e., family medicine, general internal medicine, general pediatrics

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants not accepted for admission in February may be placed on an Alternate List and are admitted as positions become available -- until the day of registration. at the end of Orientation week.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Information about the required pre-matriculation courses and important application deadlines is published in our Applicant Guide:
https://medicine.uams.edu/admissions/admissions-guide-timeline/
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No established "statute of limitations" for when pre-matriculation courses are completed but recent coursework is expected to help determine readiness to handle the rigorous medical school curriculum.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Selection is based on holistic review of whole application, scholastic attainment, performance on the MCAT, personal interviews with members of the faculty, letters, particularly from the college pre-professional advisory committees. Applicants should also demonstrate time and effort devoted to volunteerism, community service, exposure to patient care, demonstrated evidence of motivation, empathy, leadership. Selection is made without regard to race, sex, creed, national origin, age, or handicap. Unsuccessful applicants may reapply without prejudice. State law mandates we give preference to in-state applicants.  However, we may admit a limited number of non-Arkansas residents.  Preference is given to those non-Arkansas residents who have strong ties to Arkansas.  Non-Arkansans whose legal state of residence on the AMCAS application is one of the six border states, if accepted for admission, pay in-state tuition:  Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Observation/shadowing of physicians providing direct patient health care is highly recommended. Students should seek experiences in primary care and to a lesser extent, specialties in medicine. Additional experience can be gained by working in a medical setting; however, this does not replace shadowing physicians to observe the doctor-patient or doctor-family member interactions.  Although shadowing is not "required", it is always a positive factor when reviewing one's exploration of healthcare on a personal level and one's exposure to patient care.
